scheme_name: Ex-gratia for Death for the Construction Workers
description:
The Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of India to provide financial assistance to the families of construction workers who have lost their lives while engaged in construction activities. 

This scheme was launched in the year 2020 as part of the broader efforts to enhance the welfare of construction workers across the country. 

The background of this scheme stems from the recognition of the hazardous nature of construction work. 

Construction workers often face significant risks due to the nature of their work, which involves operating heavy machinery, working at heights, and exposure to various safety hazards.

The primary objective of the Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers scheme is to provide immediate financial relief to the families of deceased construction workers. 

The scheme aims to ensure that the families do not face financial hardships in the wake of the loss of their primary breadwinner. 

Under this scheme, the government provides a one-time ex-gratia payment of ₹2 lakh to the family of the deceased construction worker. 

This amount is intended to help cover immediate expenses and provide some financial stability during a difficult time.

To be eligible for this scheme, the applicant must be a registered construction worker under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996. 

The applicant must also provide proof of the worker's death while engaged in construction work. 

There are no specific age limits for the construction workers, but they must be actively registered with the appropriate state welfare board.

The income criteria for eligibility are generally aligned with the guidelines set by the respective state governments. 

Most states require that the construction worker's family income does not exceed ₹10,000 per month to qualify for the benefits under this scheme.

The application process for the Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers is straightforward. 

The family members of the deceased worker must approach the local Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

They need to fill out the application form provided by the board. 

The required documents typically include the death certificate of the worker, proof of registration as a construction worker, and identity proof of the applicant. 

In some states, additional documentation may be required, such as proof of relationship to the deceased.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the welfare board. 

The processing time may vary by state but typically takes around 30 to 45 days from the date of application submission.

Disbursement of the ex-gratia amount is usually made directly to the bank account of the eligible family member. 

The frequency of the scheme's benefits is one-time, meaning that the ex-gratia payment is made only once per deceased worker.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the respective state Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Boards. 

Each state has its own board responsible for the welfare of construction workers and the implementation of various schemes. 

For instance, the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board oversees the implementation of this scheme in the National Capital Territory of Delhi. 

The contact details for the boards can typically be found on the official state government websites.

As of October 2023, various states have reported disbursements under this scheme. 

For example, in Maharashtra, the state government has disbursed over ₹50 crore under this scheme since its inception. 

In Uttar Pradesh, the government has provided assistance to more than 5,000 families of deceased construction workers. 

The scheme has been particularly beneficial in states with high construction activity, where the risk of accidents is more pronounced.

The government has also emphasized the importance of awareness about this scheme among construction workers and their families. 

Awareness campaigns have been launched to ensure that eligible families know their rights and the benefits available to them.

In addition to the ex-gratia payment, some states have introduced complementary schemes to provide further support to the families of deceased workers. 

These may include educational assistance for children, health insurance, and skill development programs for the surviving family members.

The Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers scheme is part of a larger framework of welfare initiatives aimed at improving the living conditions of workers in the unorganized sector. 

The government recognizes that construction workers often lack access to social security benefits and safety nets.

In recent years, the government has taken significant steps to enhance the welfare of construction workers, including the establishment of the National Database for Construction Workers. 

This database aims to streamline the registration process and ensure that benefits reach the intended beneficiaries without delays.

The Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers scheme is a crucial component of this broader strategy. 

It reflects the government's commitment to safeguarding the rights and welfare of vulnerable workers in the construction industry.

In conclusion, the Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers scheme provides essential financial support to the families of construction workers who have tragically lost their lives. 

With a one-time payment of ₹2 lakh, the scheme aims to alleviate the immediate financial burden on grieving families. 

By ensuring that eligible families can access this support, the government seeks to promote social security and welfare for construction workers across India. 

This initiative is a vital step in recognizing the contributions of construction workers and addressing the risks they face in their line of work. 

The scheme not only provides financial assistance but also serves as a reminder of the need for improved safety standards and working conditions in the construction industry. 

As the government continues to implement and enhance welfare schemes, the Ex-gratia for Death for Construction Workers remains a significant measure in supporting the families of those who have dedicated their lives to building the nation.
